mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during such episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and ultimately reduces corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in INDPRO below -0.5% for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces earnings growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during INDPRO contraction episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in UNRATE above 5.0% and a fall in PAYEMS below 130,000 thousand persons in the same month signals labor market imbalances, which increase cost pressures and reduce hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with weak payroll growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in HOUST above 600 thousand units for two consecutive months signals robust housing demand, which boosts construction and related equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in FEDFUNDS above 3% and a decline in CPIAUCSL below 1.5% over the same month signals a restrictive monetary stance with falling inflation, which typically supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL < 1.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in RSAFS below $300 billion for six consecutive months signals a sharp reduction in consumer savings, which typically precedes increased consumer spending and higher earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
